import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Read the image
img = cv2.imread("grayImage.webp")
img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.imshow(img, cmap='gray')
plt.title("Original Image")
plt.grid(False)
plt.show()

# Add Guassian noise
mean = 0
sigma = 40
noise = np.random.normal(mean, sigma, img.shape)

noisy = img + noise
noisy = np.clip(noisy, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.imshow(noisy, cmap='gray')
plt.title("After Adding Gaussian Noise")
plt.grid(False)
plt.show()

# Average filter (5x5)
avg_filtered = cv2.blur(noisy, (5,5))

plt.figure(figsize=(6,5))
plt.imshow(avg_filtered, cmap='gray')
plt.title("After Average Filter")
plt.grid(False)
plt.show()
In [124]:
#  Morphological Filter (open)

kernel=np.ones((3,3),np.uint8)
morph_open = cv2.morphologyEx(noisy, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel)

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
plt.imshow(morph_open, cmap='gray')
plt.title("Morphological Opening")
plt.grid(False)

#  Morphological Filter (close)

morph_close = cv2.morphologyEx(morph_open, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
plt.imshow(morph_close, cmap='gray')
plt.title("Morphological Closing")
plt.grid(False)
plt.show()

plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)

Discussion about output image after applying each filter

  • The average filter removes some of the noise, but the image still remains noticeably noisy, and some fine details are lost. Because it simply averages neighboring pixels, any blurred or noisy region will produce a blurred result after filtering.

  • The morphological opening filter performs better at eliminating small noise elements and removes most of the isolated bright noise points while still preserving the important edges and structural details of the image.

  • Using a combination of opening followed by closing maintains both the image details and the shadow regions. Opening removes small bright noise through erosion followed by dilation, and closing then fills in small dark gaps through dilation followed by erosion, resulting in a cleaner and more visually consistent image.
